messages:
pagerbot: [PAGER] High auth 401 spike detected on auth-proxy-prod (us-west-2). 12k 401s in 10m, majority from 45.79.21.0/24. Related S3 upload detected to staging-logs-delta. Escalating to #incidents.

maria (oncall): I'm on. Seeing the same in dashboards — 401s from one ASN. Isolate and sample logs. @kevin can you pull a proxy tail?

kevin (eng-sre): grabbing tails now. Sample request: 
```
10.0.4.12 - - [10/Mar/2026:10:21:12 +0000] "POST /v1/auth HTTP/1.1" 401 125 "-" "curl/7.68.0" x-api-key: "redacted"
```

pagerbot: Alert attached: s3://staging-logs-delta/2026-03-10/debug-10-21.log (new object). md5: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184. Possible debug logging with tokens.

irene (sec): If debug logs contain tokens we need immediate key rotation for svc-infer-runner-prod and staging API keys. Also preserve all S3 objects, do not delete. Any customer-facing impact?

maria (oncall): Preliminary: small subset of beta customers using staging routing saw elevated 401s. No PII reported by support yet. We'll assume tokens in debug logs may be scoped, but proceed as if they are sensitive.

kevin (eng-sre): I've applied a temporary WAF rule to block ASN 1337 and rate-limit the offending /v1/auth path from the IP range. Seeing 70% drop in 401s already.

maria (oncall): Good. Plan: 1) Rotate service keys (svc-infer-runner-prod + staging keys). 2) Revoke all long-lived session tokens created in the past 24h. 3) Notify legal & privacy. I'll do rotation now.

maria (oncall): Running rotation — commands below (audit log will be saved):
```
# create new secret
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name /redwood/svc/infer/prod --secret-string '{"API_KEY":"NEWKEY-XXXX"}'
# propagate to infra
rdeploy secrets sync --service infer-runner --env prod
# disable old key
aws iam update-access-key --user svc-infer-runner --access-key-id AKIAOLD --status Inactive
```

kevin (eng-sre): Rolling WAF rule global and syncing proxy ACLs. Heads-up: cust-beta-07 may see 401s for ~1-2m during restart.

maria (oncall): Rotation complete. New secret live, old key disabled. Marking steps in incident runbook. :white_check_mark:

kevin (eng-sre): Confirming: 401 rate back to baseline, no new suspicious S3 objects created in the last 30m. Proxy logs show rejected requests dropping to normal.

irene (sec): Good. Next: full forensics (pull all access logs, S3 object versions, IAM last used for svc keys). I'll kick off the job and loop in legal. Do not rotate anything else until we have the scope.

legal (oncall): Acknowledged. Preparing initial customer notification template in case we need to notify. Need final scope and whether tokens gave access to customer data.

maria (oncall): Short summary for post-incident: auth-proxy-prod saw credential stuffing + debug log upload to staging S3 exposing short-lived tokens. Immediate mitigations: WAF block, key rotation, revoke recent sessions. Cust impact: potential transient 401s for small beta set, no confirmed data exfiltration yet.

sec-ops-bot: Forensics job started: job_id=forensic-1780001. Collecting proxy logs (range 2026-03-10T10:00:00Z to 2026-03-10T10:40:00Z) and S3 object metadata.

irene (sec): Handing off to sec for deeper analysis and timeline. Maria — thanks for the rapid rotation. I'll own the follow-up (postmortem + legal coordination). Meeting to review findings at 15:00 UTC.

maria (oncall): Handoff accepted. I'm clear from on-call for this handoff. Leaving notes in the incident ticket.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll keep monitoring for 24h and keep WAF rule in place until forensic says otherwise.

maria (oncall): Closing slack loop here — will update ticket with artifacts. If anything new shows up ping @irene. :lock:
